definition: OAuth 2.0 is an industry-standard authorization framework enabling third-party applications to obtain limited access to user accounts without exposing user credentials.
detailedExplanation: OAuth 2.0 defines authorization flows including Authorization Code flow with PKCE, Client Credentials, and Implicit (deprecated) flows. OpenAPI 3.0 supports oauth2 security schemes with authorizationUrl and tokenUrl.
commonMistakes: Using Implicit flow in modern applications
Not specifying scopes in OpenAPI security declarations
